speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Please tell me, how long have you been experiencing wrist pain, fever, and these skin lesions?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (GC Arthritis-Dermatitis).

Based on the history of recent camping in Minnesota, a self-resolving monoarthritis (likely a "migratory" phase), and the current presentation of oligoarticular wrist pain with fever and skin lesions, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of disseminated gonococcal infection. I would like to confirm the nature of the skin lesions and check for other joint involvement. REQUEST TEST: Urine NAAT for Gonorrhea and Chlamydia; REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up photos of the skin lesions.
